chunks: And Sahl ibn Ziyad reported it from Ahmad ibn al-Ash'ath, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, also similarly.

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ الْأَشْعَثِ: Ahmad ibn al-Ash'ath, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي نَصْر: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, a key narrator often cited in Al-Kafi
key_terms.أَيْضًا: Also/likewise, indicating this is an additional narration
key_terms.سَهْلُ بْنُ زِيَادٍ: Sahl ibn Ziyad, a prominent Shia narrator
key_terms.مِثْلَهُ: Similar to it, indicating the content matches the previously mentioned hadith

ai.seo_question: Who are the narrators in this specific chain of transmission for the hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This segment provides an alternative chain of narration (isnad) for a hadith, linking the report through Sahl ibn Ziyad to Ahmad ibn al-Ash'ath and then to Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, confirming the content is consistent with previous narrations. The inclusion of Sahl ibn Ziyad, a prominent companion of Imam al-Rida and al-Jawad, adds weight to the reliability of the transmission within the Usuli school of Shia scholarship. This multi-chain verification (tawatur) underscores the authenticity of the specific ruling or narrative associated with the chapter on 'The Fig' (At-Tin).
